newsitem.title: FINLAND: Raisio up as 96 beats expectations.
newsitem.headline: Raisio up as 96 beats expectations.

text.p: Raision Tehtaat Oy, a Finnish food and chemicals company which has invented a cholesterol-cutting margarine, said on Thursday its profit last year rose by nearly one-fifth and saw a clear improvement this year.

Raisio said 1996 profit before extraordinary items and tax was 166 million markka ($34 million) against 141 million in 1995, with sales up 22 percent at 3.9 billion, a result above most expectations which was boosted mainly by an upturn in its chemicals business.
Analysts' median forecast had been for a 148 million markka profit and tax in a 128-204 million range.
"The outlook for 1997 is clearly better than last year," CEO Matti Salminen told a news conference.
Raisio's share rose sharply in early trade but dealings were thin and brokers were unsure if gains would hold. At 0855 GMT, Raisio traded at 440.00 markka, up 16.00 markka or almost four percent.

Raisio's stock has exploded in Helsinki since this time last year, when the margarine, called Benecol, attracted heavy international interest with the share at just over 100 markka. It recently peaked at 446.50 markka, up nearly 350 percent.
Over 50 percent of Raisio's stock is now held by overseas investors.
"Expectations for billions of markka in profits are in the future and they (Raisio) said nothing about that," one broker said, adding he saw no reason for the stock's initial gain.
The results were preliminary and Raisio has not yet made a dividend proposal.
Salminen in a statement called the performance extremely satisfactory amid foreign competition, lower prices and exceptionally high research and development expenses.
Raisio's chemicals division, which produces chemicals for the pulp and paper industry, more than doubled profit after depreciation to 101 million markka from a weak 48 million in 1995.

The business was then hampered by stoppages in the pulp and paper industry and high raw material prices of latexes, Raisio said. Although stoppages continued in 1996, capacity use improved and latex raw material prices fell.

Raisio said its sales were boosted by acquisitions abroad, more exports and success on the domestic market: international sales accounted for nearly 40 percent of the total and exports rose 42 percent to 735 million markka.

"1996 will go down in the Raisio Group's history as Benecol year, such was the role of this new cholesterol-reducing margarine in increasing the group's visibility and general interest in all our sectors of operations," Salminen said.
Research and development expenses totalled 87 million markka or over two percent of turnover, with the Benecol project accounting for 22 million, Raisio said.
Raisio said it would publish final results on February 25. ($ = 4.961 Finnish Markka)
